$comment: Single source of truth for the coordinated release. The npm packages all publish at `version` (sync mode — see RELEASING.md). The model identity (which trained artifact + tokenizer the neural-weights-* packages bundle) lives under `weights`, decoupled from the artifact's historical filename. Paths are relative to the data root ($MAILWOMAN_DATA_ROOT, resolved by `dataRootPath()` — override individual files with MAILWOMAN_PUBLISH_MODEL / MAILWOMAN_PUBLISH_TOKENIZER). Bump `version` here in lockstep with the release; copy-weights.ts, the ship script, and the model card all read this instead of hardcoding the numbers.

softFeed.$comment: Soft-feed artifacts (#718 D1) materialized into each neural-weights-<locale> workspace at publish time by copy-weights.ts so the library default `loadFromWeights` feeds the channels the anchor+gazetteer-trained model expects (closing the anchor-OFF crater). The PCB1 postcode binary is built from the WOF postcode extract (per locale's country code); the gazetteer lexicon is the codex-generated repo file. Paths under `db` are relative to the data root's `wof/`. Like the weights binaries, these are skipped in CI (MAILWOMAN_SKIP_WEIGHTS_COPY) — the publish workflow places them via the HF fetch step.

postcodeDBByCountry.$comment_gb: `gb` RETURNED 2026-08-06 (ROAD_TO_V9 §1 A4) after being removed 2026-08-05 (#1467). The removal was required while the encoder's GB anchor slot was untrained (see $comment_gb_readd's history); v4.2.0-base-anchor-v2 trained the slot (Fisher receipts in the 9.0.0 lineage) and the three-part re-add below is now IN EFFECT: the en-gb card declares span_mode 'shaped', its files[] names postcode-gb.bin, and this key points at the license-clean Code-Point source. The GeoNames-lineage postalcode-gb.db stays retired.
postcodeDBByCountry.$comment_gb_readd: WHEN `gb` COMES BACK (2026-08-06, ROAD_TO_V9 §1 A4). It is no longer a one-line edit, and that is deliberate — three things move together or the release is incoherent, and each half now fails loudly on its own. (1) neural-weights-en-gb/model-card.json declares `requires.anchor.span_mode: "shaped"` (or "postal", the span mode of the postal family); without it the runtime refuses the pairing (`createScorer` throws, a parse warns) because the binary's unit keys are unreachable by the default alnum-run scan. (2) neural-weights-en-gb/package.json's `files` gains `postcode-gb.bin` — `neural/test/weights.test.ts` asserts the files entry and the card's span_mode are present together, and `lib/release-kit/pack/verify-tarball.ts` fails the publish if a literal files entry is missing from the tarball. (3) this key returns as `postalcode-gb-codepoint.db` (the license-clean OGL v3.0 Code-Point Open source, 1,749,839 keys — NOT the retired GeoNames-lineage postalcode-gb.db). `scripts/link-dev-weights.ts` already builds it in dev off the same card check, so a worktree tells you the answer before CI does.

postcodePrefixByCountry.$comment: The PFX1 postcode-prefix indexes the anchor-region prior reads (#2585), one scope per entry, copied by copy-weights.ts from the newest dated file under the data root's `postcode-prefix/` directory as `postcode-prefix-<scope>.bin`. A scope whose PFX1 header records tier `build-local` is refused: `gb-ni` is built from OpenStreetMap under ODbL and stays out of every package.

pairIndexByCountry.$comment: The placetype-pair-prior arc's PIX1 retrieval index (placetype-pair-prior arc, Task 3/8) — mirrors postcodeDBByCountry's shape exactly, but the source is a CSV of (child, parent) tuples rather than a WOF DB, and `--delta` is a REQUIRED calibrated value (no default — see `mailwoman gazetteer pair-index --help`). `source` and `banDir` are current sources, relative to the cache root's `sources/`. `boroughDB` is a WOF database filename, resolved under the data root's `db/wof/` like postcodeDBByCountry. COUNTRY-SPECIFIC BY DESIGN, same as the runtime resolver (neural/weights.ts's resolvePairIndexSibling): a locale with no entry here simply ships no pair-index sibling and the prior stays inert for it.
pairIndexByCountry.$comment_parentDelta: `parentDelta` (#46, the whole-edge parent bias) is present on us/gb/nz/fr ONLY, at the δ=5 the 2026-08-04 verdict recommended (docs/records/evals/2026-08-04-pix1-whole-edge-verdict.md). de/in/es/it deliberately omit it: no board has graded the parent side on those locales, and the D-rule's answer to an unmeasured locale is a per-locale check rather than an inherited magnitude. An ABSENT key means the shipped artifact carries no parentDelta and the parent bias is OFF for that locale — not zero.

gb.$comment: No `source`: Great Britain reads no tuple CSV. The index read HM Land Registry Price Paid Data until 2026-10-17, and packages/corpus/data/license-decisions.json refuses that source's address fields (`unchecked-access-free-gb-gb-property-building-1`); `gazetteer pair-index` now refuses a GB `--source`. The pairs are Who's On First's: the admin DB's borough pairs and the three committed JSONL files. OS Open Names pairs were measured as a replacement on the GB board and regressed more rows than this set, so they are not read (#2635).

fr.$comment: Hierarchy campaign R6 (2026-08-01). Source is the raw BAN dump (DINUM/IGN, Licence Ouverte 2.0) read through ban/sdk's cleanLieuDit — NOT WOF, whose French neighborhood records are Paris quartiers that never appear in a postal address. The line French addresses DO carry is the lieu-dit.

in.$comment: Hierarchy campaign R10 (2026-08-02). WOF-sourced (area, city) pairs with parent-alias expansion — India Post carries an area line on essentially every address, and WOF's city names lag official renames.

es.$comment: Hierarchy campaign R11 (2026-08-02). WOF-sourced pairs with parent-alias expansion; leading-postcode locale.

it.$comment: Hierarchy campaign R11 (2026-08-02). WOF-sourced pairs with parent-alias expansion; leading-postcode locale.

de.$comment: Hierarchy campaign R9 (2026-08-02). WOF-sourced (Ortsteil, Gemeinde) pairs — Deutsche Post routes 'PLZ Stadt' and carries no Ortsteil field, so there is no postal register to harvest.

us.$comment: Hierarchy campaign R5 (2026-08-01). No `source`: the US has no postal register carrying dependent localities (USPS routes city/state/ZIP), so every pair is WOF-sourced via --borough-db. Same delta/beta as GB — that is the pair the R5 bars were measured with.

assets.$comment: Where the model release lives for the demo + the CI weights pull. The release path embeds `version`; publish.yml derives the same path from the model card so CI and local stay in sync.

addressLayers.$comment: The address-layer version this release serves, by country. `mailwoman data bom` reads that version's manifest and per-region ATTRIBUTION.json from the public bucket, or from the data root when it holds the version, to list each source inside the layer with its publisher's terms. `mailwoman situs publish` prints the line to change here after it publishes a version.
